gaps.sentence: You will not pass the course unless you ___ all the assignments.
gaps.hint: unless means if not, present simple
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' introduces a negative condition and takes the present simple: complete.

gaps.sentence: I wish you ___ your shoes in the middle of the floor!
gaps.hint: irritation about a habit, wish would
gaps.explanation: 'Wish' plus 'would' expresses irritation about a habit you want changed: would not leave.

gaps.sentence: I will write down the address in case I ___ it.
gaps.explanation: 'In case' describes a precaution against a possibility and takes the present simple: forget.

gaps.sentence: In case of fire, ___ the nearest exit.
gaps.hint: in case of plus an emergency instruction
gaps.explanation: 'In case of' plus a noun introduces an emergency instruction with the imperative: use.

gaps.sentence: I wish I ___ to your advice — then I would not be in this mess.
gaps.hint: regret about the past, past perfect
gaps.explanation: 'Wish' plus the past perfect expresses regret about the past: had listened.

gaps.sentence: If only I ___ my umbrella — I am getting soaked!
gaps.hint: present regret about an earlier decision
gaps.explanation: 'If only' plus the past perfect expresses a present regret about a past decision: had brought.

gaps.sentence: If she ___ the lottery, she would travel the world.
gaps.explanation: Second conditional: if + past simple, would + infinitive.

gaps.sentence: What ___ if the bridge had collapsed?
gaps.hint: a question about an unreal past
gaps.explanation: Questions about unreal pasts use 'would have' plus the participle: would have happened.
